subject: Clarify: SOC 2 coverage for KMS custody, transient logs, snapshots & subprocessor attestations
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>
To: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@alphahealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.inference, marissa_cole@redwood.inference
Date: 2027-07-18T09:12:00Z
Subject: SOC 2 - KMS custody, transient logs, snapshots & subprocessor attestations

Jordan —

Following up on our SOC 2 onboarding checklist: we need a few clarifications to complete the subservice mapping and the bridge-letter draft for AlphaHealth. Specific asks below:

1) KMS custody/ownership: does AlphaHealth use customer-managed keys (CMK) for production encryption, or are keys escrowed/managed by your cloud provider? If CMKs are used, please confirm who holds the root key material and whether key rotation/backup processes are included in the provider's SOC 2 scope.

2) Snapshots & backups: are DB snapshots and block-storage snapshots (including encrypted backups stored in your cloud provider) covered within your cloud provider SOC 2 report? We need to know whether backup retention and restore procedures are part of the covered controls or treated as an out-of-scope operational process.

3) Transient logs/ephemeral storage: are ephemeral log streams (e.g., application logs routed through a managed log service for <30 days) considered in-scope for your provider's SOC 2? If they are excluded, please state retention windows and any downstream processors that ingest these logs.

4) Subprocessor chain: please provide the current subprocessor CSV (names, roles, location, and SOC/ISO attestation if available). We are particularly interested in any managed DB, backup, or KMS providers.

5) Audit period alignment & bridge letter: your SOC 2 Type II covers 2026-07-01 -> 2027-06-30 per our records. Can you confirm the period and provide a signed bridge letter clarifying shared vs. provider responsibilities for the items above? A short statement that the provider's report covers (or does not cover) key custody, snapshots, and logs is ideal for our auditors.

I attached our evidence checklist to show what we still need. If it's easier, we can draft the bridge letter language and send it back for signature. Would appreciate responses by end of day tomorrow — our internal audit window is tight.

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Security Partnerships | Redwood Inference
---
Attachments: redwood-soc2-evidence-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet: mapping of evidence items we request)

From: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@alphahealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>
Cc: security@alphahealth.com
Date: 2027-07-18T13:47:00Z
Subject: Re: SOC 2 - KMS custody, transient logs, snapshots & subprocessor attestations

Hannah —

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front, and I'm attaching our SOC 2 PDF and a current subprocessor export.

1) KMS custody: AlphaHealth uses provider-managed KMS for most workloads (customer-managed-key feature not enabled for your pilot environment). Key material is retained by the cloud provider; key rotation is automated by the provider. Our SOC 2 report notes KMS management procedures for the managed service — see section 4.2.

2) Snapshots & backups: Encrypted snapshots for managed DB services are covered by the provider's controls as documented in the report; however, object-store backups that are customer-initiated (ad hoc exports) are not included unless configured through the managed backup pipeline.

3) Transient logs: Short-term ephemeral logs (retention <30 days) routed to the provider-managed log service are included in the provider's monitoring control, but long-term archival (S3 exports) is a separate process and not part of that specific control.

4) Subprocessors: attaching CSV (alphahealth-subprocessors-20270718.csv). Key entries: CloudProviderX (KMS, managed DB, object store); LogCo (managed logs); BackupsRUs (snapshot replication). Where available we list attestation links column E.

5) Audit period: our current report covers 2026-07-01 -> 2027-06-30; we can provide a bridge letter confirming coverage and clarifying that KMS custody is provider-managed for the environments you requested.

I'll also attach a draft bridge letter for your review (draft_bridge_letter_alphahealth.docx). Please let me know if you want wording that explicitly enumerates "transient logs" vs "archival exports."

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Liu
Security Operations Manager, AlphaHealth
---
Attachments: AlphaHealth_SOC2_TypeII_2026-07-01_2027-06-30.pdf (PDF), alphahealth-subprocessors-20270718.csv (CSV), draft_bridge_letter_alphahealth.docx (DOCX)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.inference
Date: 2027-07-18T15:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SOC 2 - KMS custody, transient logs, snapshots & subprocessor attestations

On Jul 18, 2027, at 13:47, Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@alphahealth.com> wrote:
> Hannah —
> 
> Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front...

Thanks Jordan — useful. Hannah: two quick internal notes for the audit team before we accept the bridge language:

- We should ask Jordan to explicitly confirm whether provider-managed KMS means the provider holds raw key material and whether they perform key escrow to a separate HSM region (we need that for our key compromise scenarios).
- For snapshots: request a short statement on whether snapshot encryption keys are the same KMS tenant as DB encryption (some providers split control). If they don't, we need a compensating control.

I can propose three short sentences for the bridge letter that make these points clear. If Jordan okays, I'll push the draft to him tonight.

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Liu <jordan.liu@alphahealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.inference>, karthik_iyer@redwood.inference
Date: 2027-07-19T15:42:00Z
Subject: Re: SOC 2 - KMS custody, transient logs, snapshots & subprocessor attestations

Hannah / Karthik —

Thanks — I've updated the draft bridge letter to add explicit language on KMS custody and snapshot key partitioning. We confirmed with the provider: keys for managed DB snapshots live in the same tenant KMS, and the provider does not escrow raw key material outside the managed KMS service.

I've uploaded the signed bridge letter (scanned signature pending) and a short addendum clarifying transient log retention is handled by LogCo for up to 28 days before archival exports; archival exports are outside provider SOC scope unless processed via the managed backup pipeline.

Next steps: I'll send the signed PDF by Monday EOD for your auditors.

Jordan
---
Attachments: AlphaHealth_signed_bridge_letter_20270719.pdf (PDF), alphahealth-subprocessors-20270718.csv (CSV)

Notes: The thread contains a mix of short internal direction and vendor responses; attachments referenced above include SOC 2 report, subprocessor list, and a draft bridge letter template. The exchange will be used to finalize a bridge letter for Redwood's auditors and to map shared responsibilities for KMS, snapshots, and log retention.
